skill.name: code-analysis
skill.description: Analyze source files for non-developer readability, including naming, comments, jargon, and section documentation.
skill.summary: Scores code readability and suggests plain-language improvements for non-developer audiences.
skill.author: abereyes

content.value_statement: Code can be hard for non-developers to review when names, comments, and jargon are unclear. This skill scores readability and suggests clearer naming, comments, and documentation.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes supported source files by extension, including Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, Go, Ruby, and PHP.
Flags cryptic variable names and single-letter assignments outside common loop counters.
Checks comment ratio and long code blocks without explanatory comments.
Detects unexplained technical jargon inside comment lines.
Checks functions and classes for What, Why, and How documentation.
Outputs a human-readable report or JSON with score, issues, and suggestions.
limitations: The analyzer is regex-based and may miss language-specific edge cases.
The current script analyzes one supported file path at a time.
The focus and audience options are parsed but do not change analysis behavior.
It reviews readability only and does not test correctness, performance, or security.

use_cases.title: Prepare stakeholder-friendly code
use_cases.description: Check whether a source file uses names and comments that business reviewers can understand.

use_cases.title: Review onboarding examples
use_cases.description: Find unclear abbreviations, missing explanations, and jargon before sharing examples with new team members.

use_cases.title: Improve delivery documentation
use_cases.description: Identify functions and classes that need clearer What, Why, and How documentation before handoff.

prompt_templates.title: Check One File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use code-analysis to review src/app.py with standard strictness. Summarize the score and top readability fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one source file.

prompt_templates.title: Find Comment Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze src/service.ts and focus the summary on missing comments, unclear jargon, and documentation gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Targeted review for code that needs clearer explanations.

prompt_templates.title: Run Strict Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use strict mode on src/payment.go. List the highest-impact naming and documentation changes for a new team member.
prompt_templates.scenario: Detailed review before sharing code with a broader team.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Remediation
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze src/controller.py and group readability issues by urgency. Recommend the first three changes to make for stakeholders.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced triage for delivery or handoff.

output_examples.input: Analyze a Python service file with standard strictness.
output: The report found unclear abbreviations and several long sections without comments.
Suggested fixes included clearer names and short What, Why, and How explanations.

output_examples.input: Review a TypeScript component in strict mode.
output: The review highlighted missing function documentation and unexplained technical terms in comments.
The summary recommended adding plain-language explanations before sharing the file with new team members.

output_examples.input: Create a machine-readable readability report for one supported file.
output_examples.output: The tool can return structured results with file details, language, score, issue count, and per-issue suggestions.

best_practices: Run the analyzer on individual source files with supported extensions.
Start with standard strictness, then use strict mode for shared or critical code.
Review each suggestion in context because some technical terms may be acceptable.
anti_patterns: Do not run it on unsupported file types and expect complete results.
Do not treat the readability score as a substitute for human review.
Do not optimize only the score while ignoring whether the code is actually clearer.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It checks naming, comments, technical jargon, documentation, and overall readability score for supported source files.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it change my code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It reports readability issues and suggestions, but it does not edit files.

faq.question: Can it analyze directories?
faq.answer: The command help mentions files or directories, but the current script only fully handles one supported file path.

faq.question: Which languages are supported?
faq.answer: It supports common source extensions for Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, TSX, Java, Go, Ruby, and PHP.

faq.question: Is this a security scanner?
faq.answer: No. It is a readability analyzer and does not check vulnerabilities or malicious behavior.
